sentence: It starts at the end of a nerve.
claim: A muscle contracts when a motor nerve ending signals it at the neuromuscular junction.
source_title: Physiology, Neuromuscular Junction (StatPearls; editor P. C. Bollu, updated 17 Feb 2025)
note: Not directly stated on the page I could read. The page says botulinum toxin 'acts at the neuromuscular junction to cause muscle paralysis by inhibiting the release of acetylcholine from presynaptic motor neurons', which implies the nerve ending is what drives the muscle. The StatPearls page named earlier is blocked here and the NCBI Bookshelf copy returned a reCAPTCHA. A person should open a neuromuscular-junction page.

sentence: The nerve lets out a chemical messenger called acetylcholine.
claim: At the neuromuscular junction the motor nerve ending releases acetylcholine, a chemical messenger, into a narrow gap.
source_title: Botulinum toxin (Nigam PK, Nigam A; Indian Journal of Dermatology, 2010)
note: PMC2856357 (read 2026-11-08): 'blocking the release of acetylcholine, which is the principal neurotransmitter at the neuromuscular junction' and 'inhibiting the release of acetylcholine from presynaptic motor neurons'. 'Chemical messenger' is a plain-words gloss for neurotransmitter.

sentence: The muscle fibre gets the message, and pulls.
claim: The released acetylcholine acts on the muscle fibre to make it contract.
source_title: Physiology, Neuromuscular Junction (StatPearls; editor P. C. Bollu, updated 17 Feb 2025)
note: Implied only: the same page says blocking acetylcholine release causes muscle paralysis, so release normally makes the muscle work. Not stated as 'the muscle fibre pulls'. Needs a neuromuscular-junction source a person opens (StatPearls blocked here).

sentence: Botulinum toxin gets inside the nerve ending.
claim: Botulinum toxin acts at the neuromuscular junction; its light chain works inside the motor nerve ending.
source_title: Botulinum toxin (Nigam PK, Nigam A; Indian Journal of Dermatology, 2010)
note: PMC2856357: the toxin binds 'to high affinity receptors at the presynaptic surface of cholinergic neurones, and the toxin-receptor complex is taken up into the cell by endocytosis… the toxin escapes into the cytoplasm.'

sentence: It blocks proteins the nerve needs to send the message.
claim: The toxin's light chain interacts with SNARE proteins in the nerve ending, including SNAP-25, to prevent acetylcholine vesicles from fusing with the membrane.
source_title: Botulinum toxin (Nigam PK, Nigam A; Indian Journal of Dermatology, 2010)
note: PMC2856357: 'The light (L) chain interact[s] with different proteins (synaptosomal associated protein (SNAP) 25, vesicle associated membrane protein and syntaxin) in the nerve terminals to prevent fusion of acetylcholine vesicles with the cell membrane.' The page does NOT say 'cuts', or 'one protein', so the sample now says 'blocks proteins'. SNAP-25 is named among them. The type-A cleavage of SNAP-25 is well known but is not on the page I read: OPEN until a person opens a source that states it.

sentence: So, for a while, the message is not sent.
claim: With vesicle fusion prevented, acetylcholine is not released; the effect of type A usually lasts about three months.
source_title: Botulinum toxin (Nigam PK, Nigam A; Indian Journal of Dermatology, 2010)
note: PMC2856357: blocks 'the release of acetylcholine'; 'The weakness induced by injection with botulinum toxin A usually lasts about three months'; function recovers 'by the sprouting of nerve terminals… this usually takes two to three months'. So the line says 'for a while', not 'never'.

sentence: The skin was never the target.
claim: The toxin's effect is on the nerve-muscle junction (it blocks acetylcholine release), not on the skin itself.
source_title: Botulinum toxin (Nigam PK, Nigam A; Indian Journal of Dermatology, 2010)
note: PMC2856357: 'acts at the neuromuscular junction to cause muscle paralysis by inhibiting the release of acetylcholine'. The page does not use the phrase 'the skin is not the target'; that is the film's plain-words reading (dermatologist to confirm).
